KR-JUY-001.name_en: Chung Ju-yung: From War Deserter to Han River Miracle Architect — the 'Extreme Survival Entrepreneurship' and Government-Business Symbiosis Governance Paradigm
KR-JUY-001.description_en: Chung Ju-yung (정주영, 1915-2001) was founder of Hyundai Group and the core industrial engine of South Korea's 'Miracle on the Han River' under President Park Chung-hee. Born to a poor farming family in黄海道, North Korea, he was forcibly conscripted as war labor in 1939 and escaped back to his hometown, starting with 500,000 won to contract civil engineering projects amid post-war ruins. Chung's core philosophy was transforming 'extreme survival pressure' into 'extraordinary execution efficiency' — with extreme work ethics of '5am meetings, 8am开工', he completed South Korea's first expressway (Gyeongbu Expressway) and largest dam (Geumgang Dam) from Korean War rubble, laying the foundation for heavy industry. He institutionalized 'government-business symbiosis': deep cooperation with Park Chung-hee's regime, trading state-led industrialization strategy for government contracts and protection, while completing Korea's industrial upgrade from civil engineering to steel, shipbuilding, and automobiles through vertical chain integration ('Hyundai Construction → Hyundai Heavy Industries → Hyundai Motor'). Chung is the sole East Asian sample of mode 34 (Strategic Prediction) in 'from low-end contracting to heavy industry full-chain layout' scenarios, and the unique representative of mode 12 (Systems Thinking) in 'institutionalizing government-business symbiosis' scenarios.
KR-JUY-001.reason_en: Chung Ju-yung fills Protreptic's gap in 'East Asian government-business symbiosis industrialization path'. His extreme life trajectory from war deserter to industrial empire builder demonstrates how to achieve industrial leapfrogging through 'extreme survival entrepreneurship' under extreme resource scarcity; also the sole Korean sample of mode 34 in 'from civil engineering to heavy industry full-chain' scenarios. His government-business symbiosis model is irreplaceable for understanding the operational mechanisms of East Asian developmental states and provides a classic case study for industrial policy in late-developing nations.
steps_en: Step 1 (Mode 34 Strategic Prediction): Crisis identification and opportunity lock — amid Korean War rubble, accurately judged that national reconstruction demand far exceeded private consumption needs, investing all 500,000 won in civil engineering contracting rather than consumer goods

Step 2 (Mode 12 Systems Thinking): Government-business symbiosis architecture — deep cooperation with Park Chung-hee regime, trading 'state-led industrialization' for government mega-project contracts (Geumgang Dam, Gyeongbu Expressway), while building subsidiary companies in steel and heavy industry through profit reinvestment

Step 3 (Mode 20 Value Chain Restructuring): Vertical chain integration — upgrading from pure civil engineering contractor to complete industrial chain of 'construction→steel→shipbuilding→automobiles', each phase providing foundation for the next

Step 4 (Mode 38 Testing Waters): Gradual industrial upgrading — starting from lowest-end civil contracting, progressively entering heavy industry (Hyundai Heavy Industries 1972), shipbuilding, and finally automobiles, each step built on accumulated capital and technology from prior phases

Step 5 (Paradigm Solidification): Han River miracle engine — condensing 'extreme survival→government-business symbiosis→chain integration→gradual upgrading' into an operable template for Korean industrialization, becoming a classic sample of developmental state theory

KR-JUY-001.case_en: In 1972, Hyundai Heavy Industries built a shipyard by clearing mountains and filling the sea at Pohang Harbor. Chung personally directed workers to carry stones basket-by-basket with shovels. At that time, Korea had no shipbuilding technology foundation whatsoever, but he used 'national need' as his strategic pivot, importing Japanese technology and training Korean engineers, completing Asia's largest shipyard in just 3 years. The yard delivered the world's first 450,000-ton VLCC in 1975, marking Korea's entry into the world's top shipbuilding tier. Hyundai Heavy Industries has ranked #1 in global shipbuilding output for 30 consecutive years, becoming the most symbolic industrial totem of the 'Han River Miracle'. In his later years, Chung also ran for South Korean president as an independent candidate in 1992, receiving 48.6% of the vote — demonstrating a unique path from business leader to political arena.

GH-NKR-001.name_en: Nkrumah: From Colonial Periphery to Pan-African Unity — the 'Continental Federation Construction' and Political Mobilization Governance Paradigm
GH-NKR-001.description_en: Kwame Nkrumah (1909-1972) was Ghana's first Prime Minister (1957-1960) and President (1960-1966), the theoretical founder and practical leader of Pan-Africanist movements. Born in a small village in southern Gold Coast (now Ghana), during his US studies he was exposed to African diaspora political thought from Du Bois, Marcus Garvey and George Padmore. In 1945 he organized the Fifth Pan-African Congress (Manchester), first writing 'colonial people's self-rule' into international political agenda. Nkrumah's core thinking contribution was elevating 'Pan-Africanism' from academic theory of diaspora intellectuals to an operable 'continental federation construction method' — through a three-stage leap ('Gold Coast independence → Ghana-Guinea Union → founding of Organization of African Unity (OAU)'), he constructed an operational framework for African political unity. He proposed the radical vision of 'United States of Africa', advocating economic self-sufficiency through political unity. Nkrumah is the sole West African sample of mode 12 (Systems Thinking) in 'cross-sovereign state federation construction' scenarios, and the unique representative of mode 6 (United Front) in 'Pan-African transnational political alliance' scenarios. His concept of 'neo-colonialism' — 'formal independence, substantive control' — became the core analytical tool of post-colonial studies.
GH-NKR-001.reason_en: Nkrumah fills Protreptic's West African gap in 'Pan-African political engineering'. He is the sole sample of mode 12 (Systems Thinking) in 'cross-sovereign state federation construction', demonstrating how to integrate fragmented African political forces into a unified continental governance framework; also the global benchmark of mode 6 (United Front) in 'Pan-African transnational alliances'. His neo-colonialism theory provides irreplaceable analytical tools for understanding imperialism's operation in the post-colonial era, with continuing theoretical guidance value for contemporary African integration (African Union, regional economic communities).
steps_en: Step 1 (Mode 6 United Front): Pan-African intellectual alliance — organized 'West African National Council (WANC)' in US and UK, 1945 Manchester Fifth Pan-African Congress first writing 'colonial people's self-rule' into international political agenda, establishing cross-colonial intellectual unified action framework

Step 2 (Mode 34 Strategic Prediction): Independence path design — judging that 'Gold Coast is the only West African colony with modern educational foundation and political organization', using it as springboard to drive continent-wide independence wave: 'Ghana's independence means nothing unless it leads to the total liberation of Africa'

Step 3 (Mode 12 Systems Thinking): Continental federation construction — proposing 'United States of Africa' vision, establishing Ghana-Guinea-Mali Union (1961), pushing to found Organization of African Unity (OAU, 1963 Addis Ababa) as continental political coordination mechanism

Step 4 (Mode 31 Framing Effect): Neo-colonialism critique — in 'Neo-Colonialism: The Last Stage of Imperialism' (1965) proposing the 'formal independence, substantive control' concept, revealing how former colonies remain controlled by original colonizers economically, monetarily and culturally

Step 5 (Paradigm Solidification): Pan-African political engineering — condensing 'intellectual alliance→independence springboard→continental federation→neo-colonial critique' into an operational framework for post-colonial African political unity
GH-NKR-001.expected_en: Master Nkrumah's intellectual evolution from West African youth leader to Pan-African movement theorist; understand how 'continental federation construction' operationalizes African political unity in the post-colonial era; evaluate neo-colonialism theory's continuing impact on contemporary international relations research.
GH-NKR-001.case_en: On March 6, 1957 at midnight, the 28-year-old Nkrumah announced Ghana's independence (formerly Gold Coast) in Accra, becoming the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence after WWII. He declared: 'Ghana's independence is meaningless unless it leads to the total liberation of Africa.' He then pushed for an African-Malayan Association (1960), established the Ghana-Guinea Union with Guinean President Sékou Touré (1958), and successfully convened the first African Heads of State Conference in Ethiopia (1963), founding the Organization of African Unity (OAU). His 'Africa Freedom' magazine and Nkrumah Pan-African Institute became centers for disseminating Pan-African thought. In February 1966, during a state visit to China when a military coup occurred in Ghana, he was exiled to Guinea where Sékou Touré bestowed upon him the title 'People's President'. Although his later rule turned toward personal dictatorship, his Pan-Africanist thought has irreplaceable theoretical foundation for the contemporary African Union (AU) and 'Africa's problems solved by Africans' philosophy.

CD-LUM-001.name_en: Lumumba (Patrice): From Colonial Clerk to National Liberation — the 'Sovereignty Return' and Anti-Imperial Struggle Governance Paradigm
CD-LUM-001.description_en: Patrice Émery Lumumba (1925-1961), commonly translated as 'Lumumba' in Chinese (referred to as '普利瓦' in this task) — first Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of Congo (1960), one of Africa's most radical revolutionary leaders in nationalist liberation movements. Born to an ordinary farming family in Kasai region, southern Congo, he started as a post office clerk within the Belgian colonial bureaucracy in the 1940s, self-taught French and Dutch, becoming one of the few Africans with administrative capability in the colony. Lumumba's core thinking contribution was elevating 'national liberation' from colonial gift narrative to an operable 'Sovereignty Return method' — through a four-stage path ('MNC establishment→1958 Brussels Pan-African Conference→independence negotiation→anti-imperial struggle'), he completed Congo's political autonomy institutional design at the final moment of Belgian colonial rule. His 'Sovereignty Return' emphasizes: true independence is not power voluntarily ceded by colonizers, but sovereignty forced from the colonial power through 'irreversible political action' by the colonized people. Lumumba is the sole Central African sample of mode 34 (Strategic Prediction) in 'post-colonial sovereignty reconstruction' scenarios, and the unique representative of mode 19 (Nonviolent Resistance) in 'anti-imperial political mobilization' scenarios. His assassination (1961, conspiracy between Belgian agents and Congolese separatists) became the bloodiest turning point in African decolonization history.
CD-LUM-001.reason_en: Lumumba fills Protreptic's Central African gap in 'anti-imperial struggle sovereignty reconstruction path'. He is the sole sample of mode 34 (Strategic Prediction) in Congo decolonization scenarios, demonstrating how to transform 'limited knowledge within colonial bureaucracy' into 'irreversible political autonomy action'; also the global benchmark of mode 19 (Nonviolent Resistance) in 'anti-imperial political mobilization' scenarios. His sovereignty return theory has irreplaceable research value for understanding imperialism's operation mechanisms in the post-colonial era, African liberation movement political strategies, providing a classic case for contemporary anti-neocolonial struggles.
steps_en: Step 1 (Mode 34 Strategic Prediction): Political awakening and organization — starting as post office clerk in Belgian colonial bureaucracy (1947), self-taught French and Dutch, identifying the structural contradiction of 'colonizers' dependence on colonial administration', secretly establishing Mouvement National Congolais (MNC) from 1956

Step 2 (Mode 19 Nonviolent Resistance): Brussels Declaration — representing Congo at Ghana Accra Pan-African Conference in 1958, delivering the declaration 'the Congolese people cannot continue to accept a regime that strips them of their dignity, freedom and sovereignty', marking the public emergence of Congo's independence movement

Step 3 (Mode 6 United Front): Independence negotiation — at the 1960 Belgium-Congo roundtable conference, refusing colonialists' 'gradual independence' framework, demanding immediate complete sovereignty transfer; rapidly forming coalition government after just 6 weeks of elections, becoming first Prime Minister

Step 4 (Mode 31 Framing Effect): Anti-imperial sovereignty reconstruction — facing Katanga secession (Belgian-backed), UN peacekeeping intervention, CIA subversion after independence, delivering 'Congo Independence Declaration' (June 30, 1960), directly challenging Belgian King Baudouin's 'you have finally gained freedom' colonial narrative

Step 5 (Paradigm Solidification): Sovereignty return method — condensing 'political awakening→public declaration→independence negotiation→anti-imperial reconstruction' into an operable template for post-colonial African sovereignty struggle

CD-LUM-001.case_en: On June 30, 1960, during Congo's independence ceremony, after Belgian King Baudouin delivered his colonial praising speech, the 29-year-old Lumumba, uninvited to the podium, delivered a world-shaking 'Congo Independence Declaration': 'Without the suffering under colonial rule there would be no independence today; what we see is not a gift but the result of struggle... The Congolese people won their dignity with blood.' He then faced Katanga secessionist Moïse Tshombe (Belgian army-backed), UN Secretary-General Hammarskjöld's 'peacekeeping' intervention, and CIA subversion operations, insisting on Congo's complete sovereignty. Dismissed by President Kasa-Vubu in September 1960, then imprisoned by the army and secretly transferred to Katanga. On January 17, 1961, Lumumba was executed under Belgian agent surveillance. A UN 2001 report acknowledged Belgium bore 'moral responsibility' for Lumumba's death. His last words: 'You think you will bury me, but the seeds have been sown' became an immortal symbol of African anti-imperial struggle.

JP-SAS-001.name_en: Saigō Takamori: From Satsuma Samurai to Meiji Restoration — 'Bushidō Revival Method' and Moral Politics Engineering Paradigm (recorded as 笹木儿 in batch plan)
JP-SAS-001.description_en: Saigō Takamori (1828-1877), courtesy name Yoshinoshige, was one of the Three Great Nobles of Japan's Meiji Restoration. Born to a poor samurai family in Satsuma (Kagoshima), he rose through the sonnō jōi movement, taisei hōkan (return of government), and political restructuring to become a central architect of modern Japan. Saigō's core contribution was engineering 'Bushidō revival' from feudal loyalty into actionable modern political morality — across four phases: anti-shogunate revolution, Meiji governance construction, continental policy disputes, and the Satsuma Rebellion martyrdom. He is the key Japanese sample of mode 19 (Non-Violent Resistance) in 'feudal samurai to modern politician transformation' and the unique representative of mode 31 (Framing Effect) in 'traditional morality modern reconstruction.' His Satsuma Rebellion (1877), where imperial forces fought former samurai allies, became the final chapter of Japan's transition from feudal to modern state. His 'three deaths, seven lives' bushidō legacy provides irreplaceable insights into East Asian modernization tensions between tradition and modernity.
JP-SAS-001.reason_en: Saigō Takamori fills Protreptic's Japanese gap in 'feudal samurai modernization moral engineering.' His extreme trajectory from Satsuma retainer to Meiji architect to rebel martyr demonstrates how 'Bushidō revival' operationalizes political morality during social upheaval; also the only complete Japanese sample of mode 19 in 'traditional elite to modern state-builder transformation.' His Satsuma Rebellion and 'three deaths, seven lives' spirit provide irreplaceable insights into East Asian modernization tensions between tradition and modernity, offering classic case studies for post-feudal elite transformation globally.
steps_en: Step 1 (Mode 19 Non-Violent Resistance): Anti-shogunate movement and sonnō jōi — from Satsuma retainer, through secret alliance with Chōshū (Satsuma-Chōsū Alliance, 1866), shifting framework from 'revere emperor expel barbarians' to support shogunate then reverse,促成萨长合作 through Sakamoto Ryōma's mediation

Step 2 (Mode 31 Framing Effect): Meiji governance and han abolition — as one of Three Great Nobles participating in 1868 political restoration,推动 taisei hōkan (return of government), reconstructing Japanese political legitimacy through 'emperor direct rule' framework; voluntarily surrendered domain in 1871, sacrificing himself for modern state architecture

Step 3 (Mode 7 Strategic Prediction): Continental policy and Korean expedition — participated in Seikanron debate (1873) advocating Korean military action to divert domestic discontent; after losing within Meiji government, retired to Kagoshima and established private schools training young samurai

Step 4 (Mode 34 Strategic Prediction): Satsuma Rebellion and bushidō martyrdom — 1877 rebellion against Meiji government's samurai privilege abolition (sword ban, shizoku pension termination), leading 20,000 former samurai against imperial army's 100,000; died by seppuku at Shiroyama; his final verses embodying bushidō's last stand

Step 5 (Paradigm Solidification): Bushidō revival — condensing 'anti-shogunate → Meiji governance → Korean dispute → Satsuma martyrdom' into an operable moral engineering template for feudal elite to modern state transformation

JP-SAS-001.case_en: Born January 23, 1828 to a lower-ranking samurai family in Satsuma (Kagoshima). Childhood name Okichi, adopted to the Saigō family due to frailty. Inherited father's position in 1854, forming the 'Satsuma Three' (with Ōkubo Toshimichi and Kido Takayoshi). Participated in sonnō jōi movement during Ikedaya Incident (1862), exiled to Sata misaki for three years. Escaped wounded from Ikedaya Incident (1864). Pardoned in 1865, returned to politics, forged secret Satsuma-Chōshū alliance. Forced Tokugawa Yoshinobu's taisei hōkan (1867) with Ōkubo. As Western Army commander in Boshin War (1868), defeated former shogunate forces. Resigned as Home Minister after han abolition (1871), retired to Kagoshima. Founded private schools training ~6,000 young samurai. Seikanron debate failure (1873) led to complete withdrawal from central politics, but secretly planned Korean expedition. February 1877 launched Satsuma Rebellion with ~40,000 former samurai against imperial forces. After 23-day siege at Shiroyama, died by seppuku September 24. Posthumously pardoned in 1883, bronze statue erected at Toyomi-temple, revered as 'the last samurai.'

UZ-ULU-001.name: Ulugh Beg
UZ-ULU-001.name_en: Ulugh Beg: The Samarkand Observatory — 'Scientific Revolution Method' and Islamic Renaissance Governance Paradigm
UZ-ULU-001.description_en: Mirza Muhammad Taragai ulugh Beg (1394-1449) was the third ruler of the Timurid Empire, governor of Samarkand (1409-1449), and a great astronomer-ruler. Grandson of Timur, son of Sultan Muhammad. Ulugh Beg's core contribution was engineering 'Islamic Renaissance' from cultural ornamentation into actionable scientific revolution — across four phases: observatory construction, stellar catalog compilation, mathematical innovation, and educational systematization. He built the world's largest mural quadrant (40m radius) in Samarkand, personally compiling the 'Zij-i Sultani' (1437) containing precise positions of 1,018 stars (superior to Ptolemy's Almagest accuracy), correcting precession and obliquity values. Ulugh Beg is the key Central Asian sample of mode 34 (Strategic Prediction) in 'scientific revolution engineering' and the unique representative of mode 12 (Systems Thinking) in 'cross-cultural scientific knowledge integration.' His Zij-i Sultani directly influenced Copernicus and Kepler, serving as crucial knowledge source for European Renaissance astronomy. His work provides irreplaceable insights into how scientific revolutions occur within Islamic civilization and cross-cultural knowledge transmission mechanisms.
UZ-ULU-001.reason_en: Ulugh Beg fills Protreptic's Central Asian gap in 'Islamic civilization scientific revolution engineering.' His unique experience as a ruler personally conducting astronomy demonstrates how scientific revolutions occur in non-European civilizations; also the sole Central Asian sample of mode 34 in 'cross-century scientific knowledge transmission and transcendence.' His Zij-i Sultani's indirect contribution to the Copernican Revolution, and his scientific educational center in Central Asia, provide irreplaceable insights into Islamic civilization knowledge transmission.

Step 2 (Mode 12 Systems Thinking): Cross-cultural knowledge integration — synthesized Persian, Arabic, Indian and Chinese (absorbed by Islamic world) astronomical knowledge; unified observation standards; invited astronomers from Baghdad, Samarkand, Bukhara for 30 years (1420-1449) of continuous data collection

Step 3 (Mode 20 Value Chain Reconstruction): Zij-i Sultani compilation — personally verified every star's observational data, compiling 'Zij-i Sultani' (Sultan's Tables) with precise positions of 1,018 stars; corrected Ptolemy's precession value (from 50.8 to 49.76 seconds, near modern 49.83) and obliquity

Step 4 (Mode 7 Strategic Prediction): Madrasah educational system — established Madrasah-i-Ulug Beg in Samarkand, integrating astronomy, mathematics and jurisprudence into systematic education;培养新一代伊斯兰学者 including al-Kashi's successors

Step 5 (Paradigm Solidification): Scientific revolution method — condensing 'observatory → knowledge integration → stellar tables → educational system' into an operable template for scientific revolution within Islamic civilization

UZ-ULU-001.case_en: Born March 22, 1394 in Samarkand, grandson of Timur. At age 7 accompanied grandfather on Indian expedition; inherited Samarkand governorship after father's death in 1409. Transformed Samarkand into Islamic world scientific center during his rule (1409-1449). Began observatory construction in 1420, deploying massive resources for 40m mural quadrant. Personally participated in 30 years of astronomical observation, compiling 'Zij-i Sultani' (completed 1437) with precise positions of 1,018 stars, superior to Ptolemy's Almagest accuracy. Corrected precession to 49.76 seconds (modern: 49.83), obliquity to 23°30'. Inherited Timurid Empire in 1447 but was forced to abandon some heterodox scientific activities under pressure from conservative ulema. Overthrown and executed in 1449 by his son Abd al-Latif's coup. His observatory and stellar tables were partially lost in subsequent political turmoil, but copies survived to India (Jaisalmer observatory) and Europe. Copernicus cited Ulugh Beg's data multiple times in 'De Revolutionibus'; Tycho Brahe also referenced his observations.

US-PD-001.name_en: Peter Drucker: Founder of Modern Management — 'Knowledge Worker Management Method' and Innovation Governance Paradigm
US-PD-001.description_en: Peter F. Drucker (1909-2005) was an Austrian-American management consultant, author and educator, universally recognized as 'the father of modern management.' Born to a Viennese intellectual family (mother was a pianist, father involved in cultural publishing), educated in Austria and UK before emigrating to the US. Drucker's core contribution was engineering 'management' from enterprise operational technique into actionable modern governance — across four phases: Management by Objectives (MBO), knowledge worker theory, decentralized organization, and innovation/entrepreneurship. His concepts of 'Management by Objectives (MBO),' 'knowledge worker' definition, and 'the purpose of a business is to create customers' revolutionized organizational governance logic. Drucker is the key American sample of mode 12 (Systems Thinking) in 'organizational governance engineering' and the unique representative of mode 34 (Strategic Prediction) in 'knowledge economy era management paradigm shift.' His 'The Practice of Management' (1954) established modern management as a discipline, providing irreplaceable insights into knowledge economy organizational governance.
US-PD-001.reason_en: Peter Drucker fills Protreptic's American gap in 'knowledge economy era management engineering.' His cross-cultural journey from European intellectual to American management master demonstrates how 'management' operationalizes organizational governance in the knowledge economy; also the only complete American sample of mode 12 in 'knowledge worker management paradigm.' His MBO theory and knowledge worker concept provide irreplaceable insights into modern organizational governance for global corporate management transformation.
steps_en: Step 1 (Mode 34 Strategic Prediction): Management by Objectives theory — identified 'limitations of traditional Taylor scientific management'; in 'The Practice of Management' (1954) proposed MBO concept: vertical decomposition through 'organizational → departmental → individual goals' and horizontal coordination via 'autonomous self-control', achieving paradigm shift from control to autonomy

Step 2 (Mode 12 Systems Thinking): Knowledge worker theory — in 'Management of the Post-Society' (1973) identified 'knowledge workers replacing manual laborers as core economic productivity'; established management principles for knowledge workers: self-management capability, results orientation, continuous learning

Step 3 (Mode 20 Value Chain Reconstruction): Decentralized organization design — in 'Management: Tasks, Responsibilities, Practices' (1973) proposed 'decentralized federation' model: decomposing large organizations into manageable autonomous units (Strategic Business Units), each bearing profit responsibility, headquarters focused on strategic planning

Step 4 (Mode 31 Framing Effect): Innovation and entrepreneurship engineering — in 'Innovation and Entrepreneurship' (1985) proposed 'systematic innovation': innovation is not genius inspiration but manageable engineering system; identified 7 sources of innovation opportunity (unexpected events, incongruities, process needs, etc.), transforming innovation from romantic narrative to actionable governance tool

Step 5 (Paradigm Solidification): Knowledge worker management — condensing 'MBO → knowledge worker theory → decentralized organization → innovation engineering' into an operable template for knowledge economy era management transformation

US-PD-001.case_en: Born November 19, 1909 in Vienna; father August Drucker was cultural publisher, mother Anna (pianist). Studied international law at Berlin University and jurisprudence at Frankfurt. Emigrated to US in 1931, working as journalist and bond analyst. Joined Greenwald Trust Fund (later NYSE-listed) in 1937, beginning management research. Conducted field management studies at General Motors (1940s) and GE, establishing his empiricist methodology. Published 'The Practice of Management' in 1954, first proposing MBO concept — universally recognized as founding work of modern management. Published 39 books over 39 years including 'The Age of Discontinuity' (1980), 'Post-Capitalist Society' (1993). Mentored Jack Welch, Andy Grove and multiple generations of CEOs. His core propositions — 'the purpose of business is to create customers' and 'management is defining the mission and inspiring/organizing people to achieve it' — have become basic common sense in corporate management. Died November 11, 2005 in Claremont, California, aged 95.

US-HK-001.name_en: Henry Kissinger: From Nazi Refugee to Great Power Game — 'Balance of Power Realism Method' and Diplomatic Engineering Paradigm
US-HK-001.description_en: Henry Alfred Kissinger (1923-2023) was a German-American diplomat, political scientist and advisor, serving as Nixon/Ford National Security Advisor (1969-1975) and Secretary of State (1973-1977). Born to a Frankfurt Jewish family, he emigrated to the US in 1938 to escape Nazi persecution. Kissinger's core contribution was engineering 'Balance of Power Realism' from classical international relations theory into actionable diplomacy — across four phases: Vietnam negotiations, China opening, US-Soviet détente, and Middle East shuttle diplomacy. His 'triangular diplomacy' concept — leveraging US-China-Soviet tripartite balance to maximize American strategic space — became the classic operational model for great power games. Kissinger is the key American sample of mode 34 (Strategic Prediction) in 'Cold War great power coordination engineering' and the unique representative of mode 12 (Systems Thinking) in 'multilateral diplomatic system reconstruction.' His 'Realpolitik' methodology provides irreplaceable insights into great power relations operations and international order transformation pathways.
US-HK-001.reason_en: Henry Kissinger fills Protreptic's American gap in 'Cold War great power coordination engineering.' His extreme trajectory from Nazi refugee to Secretary of State demonstrates how 'balance of power realism' operationalizes diplomacy in complex international structures; also the only complete American sample of mode 34 in 'US-China-Soviet triangular strategic application.' His China opening, Vietnam peace negotiations and shuttle diplomacy provide irreplaceable insights into great power relations for contemporary international order reconstruction.
steps_en: Step 1 (Mode 34 Strategic Prediction): Vietnam peace negotiation engineering — identified 'US military superiority in Vietnam cannot translate to political victory'; through secret Paris negotiations (1969-1972) with North Vietnam and South Vietnamese government, 'linkage strategy' combining military pressure, diplomatic negotiations and economic aid; ultimately reaching Paris Peace Accords (1973), preserving US international credibility through 'honorable exit' framework

Step 2 (Mode 12 Systems Thinking): China opening and triangular diplomacy — judged 'Sino-Soviet split is America's most important strategic opportunity'; through Pakistani President Yahya Khan secret channel (Kissinger's secret visit 1971), Nixon's China visit (1972) signed Shanghai Communiqué, establishing US-China-Soviet triangular framework; leveraging Sino-Soviet tensions to balance USSR, dramatically altering Cold War strategic landscape

Step 3 (Mode 20 Value Chain Reconstruction): US-Soviet détente and arms control — promoted 'Strategic Arms Limitation Talks (SALT I, 1972)' and détente policy framework; transformed nuclear arms race from unlimited confrontation to manageable competition; simultaneously promoted 'Middle East shuttle diplomacy' (post-1973 Yom Kippur War), establishing disengagement agreements between Egypt and Israel

Step 4 (Mode 31 Framing Effect): Open policy and Third World strategy — established 'Realistic Intervention' framework between non-interference and intervention: supported Chilean military coup ousting Allende (1973), promoted Angolan proxy war, established 'strategic resource acquisition → anti-communist containment' framework in Africa; pragmatism replacing ideological confrontation

Step 5 (Paradigm Solidification): Balance of power realism — condensing 'Vietnam negotiations → China opening → US-Soviet détente → shuttle diplomacy' into an operable template for great power diplomatic engineering

US-HK-001.case_en: Born May 27, 1923 to a Frankfurt Jewish family; father was librarian. Emigrated to New York in 1938 with family to escape Nazi persecution, placed in immigrant shelter. Met companions at Brooklyn High School then enlisted (1943), joining Counter Intelligence Corps (CIC) by special dispensation. Post-war PhD at Harvard under Hans Morgenthau, earned doctorate 1950. Established international relations scholar reputation through articles in New York Times and Foreign Affairs. Appointed National Security Advisor by Nixon 1969; secret Beijing visit (July 1971) arranged Nixon's China visit. 1972 accompanied Nixon to China, signing Shanghai Communiqué; awarded Nobel Peace Prize same year (shared with North Vietnamese representative Le Duc Tho for Vietnam ceasefire agreement). As Secretary of State promoted US-Soviet SALT I (1972) and Middle East shuttle diplomacy. Post-1973 Yom Kippur War facilitated Egyptian-Israeli disengagement agreements. Supported Chilean military coup ousting Allende (1973), sparking US domestic controversy. Continued as Secretary of State under Ford until 1977 Carter inauguration. Thereafter became one of most influential international consultants, advising multinational corporations and governments worldwide. Died November 29, 2023 in Connecticut at age 99.

SA-MAR-001.description_en: José de San Martín (1778-1850), Argentine general and national hero, core leader of South American independence movements. He led the Army of the Andes across the mountains to liberate Chile and Peru, jointly laying the foundation for South American independence with Bolívar. San Martín's strategic vision, military prowess, and commitment to freedom made him one of the most internationally minded revolutionaries in Latin American independence. His voluntary yielding to Bolívar demonstrated political wisdom transcending personal power.
SA-MAR-001.reason_en: San Martín represents the paradigm of combining military liberation with political wisdom in Latin American independence movements. His crossing of the Andes Mountains was a feat in military history, and his liberation of Chile at the Battle of Chacabuco and the decision to liberate Peru demonstrated exceptional strategic vision. As one of the three great leaders of South American independence, his transnational liberation strategy had an irreversible impact on Latin America's political landscape.
steps_en: Study San Martín's early Spanish military career and exposure to French revolutionary ideas
Analyze the strategic planning for Chilean liberation after returning to Argentina in 1812
Explore the 1817 crossing of the Andes by the Army of the Andes and the Battle of Chacabuco
Evaluate the historical significance and political impact of entering Lima in 1821 to declare Peruvian independence
Summarize the political wisdom and revolutionary legacy of yielding to Bolívar at the Guayaquil Conference in 1822
SA-MAR-001.expected_en: Master San Martín's strategic thought as the core leader of South American independence, understand the military miracle and political significance of the Andean expedition, and evaluate his profound impact on Latin American independence格局 and modern state formation.
SA-MAR-001.case_en: In February 1817, San Martín led an Army of the Andes of 6,000 soldiers across mountain passes at 4,000 meters altitude, completing one of the most spectacular marches in military history under extreme cold and hypoxia. Subsequently defeating Spanish forces at the Battle of Chacabuco on February 24, 1817, liberating Chile. In July 1821, entering Lima to declare Peruvian independence and establishing a protectorate system. In July 1822, after meeting with Bolívar at Guayaquil, he voluntarily retired to France, entrusting the South American liberation cause to his successors.
SA-MAR-001.cross_cultural_impact: South American independence leader, cross-continental liberation strategist

MY-LON-001.description_en: Tunku Abdul Rahman (1903-1990), Malaysia's first Prime Minister (1957-1970), honored as the 'Father of Independence.' He led peaceful independence negotiations under British colonial rule, establishing a Malaysian federal system that integrated the plural social structures of Malays, Chinese, and Indians. He was an active advocate of the Non-Aligned Movement and one of the founding members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). Tunku was known for his moderate and pragmatic diplomatic style, respect for multiculturalism, and pursuit of peaceful independence.
MY-LON-001.reason_en: Tunku Abdul Rahman represents the paradigm of achieving independence through peaceful negotiations in post-colonial Southeast Asia. He skillfully balanced plural ethnic interests, establishing a federal state framework that laid the foundation for Malaysia's multicultural coexistence. As an ASEAN founder and Non-Aligned Movement member, his diplomatic wisdom had a profound impact on Southeast Asian regional cooperation.
steps_en: Study Tunku Abdul Rahman's legal education at Cambridge University and his political awakening
Analyze the peaceful struggle strategy of leading Malaya's independence negotiations from 1946-1955
Explore the historical significance and federal system design of the August 31, 1957 Malaya independence declaration
Evaluate the political decision of the 1963 Malaysian Federation establishment and merger with Singapore
Summarize his diplomatic legacy of initiating the Non-Aligned Movement in 1957 and co-founding ASEAN in 1967
MY-LON-001.expected_en: Master Tunku Abdul Rahman's peaceful nation-building philosophy as Malaysia's Father of Independence, understand the federal governance model of multicultural societies, and evaluate his contributions to Southeast Asian regional cooperation (ASEAN) and the Non-Aligned Movement.
MY-LON-001.case_en: On August 31, 1957, Tunku Abdul Rahman waved his fist at Bukit Jalil Stadium in Kuala Lumpur shouting 'Merdeka!' (Independence), declaring the Federation of Malaya's formal independence from British colonial rule. Subsequently in 1963, he promoted the establishment of the Malaysian Federation, uniting Malaya, Singapore, Sabah, and Sarawak into one nation. In 1957 he initiated the Non-Aligned Movement, advocating that small and medium countries maintain independent diplomatic stances amid great power competition. In 1967, he participated in signing the Bangkok Declaration, becoming one of ASEAN's five founding members.
MY-LON-001.cross_cultural_impact: Southeast Asian independence leader, ASEAN founding father, Non-Aligned Movement advocate

VN-HO-001.description_en: Ho Chi Minh (1890-1969), founder of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam and chairman of the Workers' Party of Vietnam, a core leader of Southeast Asian anti-colonial struggle. He traveled to France, China and Thailand in his youth to study revolutionary thought, returning to Vietnam in 1941 to establish the Viet Minh organization and lead a 30-year struggle against French and American forces. The victory at Dien Bien Phu ended French colonial rule, and the 1954 Geneva Accords recognized Vietnamese independence. His 'Bamboo Diplomacy' strategy—firm roots like bamboo roots, flexible leaves like bamboo leaves—became classic wisdom for how small nations survive amid great power competition. When he died in 1969, the goal of northern-southern unification remained unrealized, but his spiritual heritage became the foundation for eventual reunification.
VN-HO-001.reason_en: Ho Chi Minh represents the highest paradigm of Asian anti-colonial independence struggle. Growing up in the French colonial environment, he became the most resolute anti-colonial leader; his 'Bamboo Diplomacy' thought—firm foundation, flexible adaptation—is a classic contribution to the philosophy of small-nation survival. The Dien Bien Phu victory, defeating French colonial forces with inferior兵力, demonstrated the feasibility of people's war theory; his strategic resolve in long-term confrontation with a world superpower is an essential case study for asymmetric warfare.
steps_en: Study Ho Chi Minh's early life in Nghe An province, Vietnam and his French colonial education background
Analyze the revolutionary thought formation process during 1911 departure from Vietnam and time in France, Britain, America
Explore 1941 return to Vietnam establishing the Viet Minh and strategic planning for anti-French struggle
Evaluate the significance of the 1954 Dien Bien Phu victory and historical impact of the Geneva Accords
Summarize 'Bamboo Diplomacy' strategic thought, anti-American struggle and the spiritual legacy of north-south unification
VN-HO-001.expected_en: Master Ho Chi Minh's strategic thought as the core leader of Vietnam's independence movement, understand the historical significance of Dien Bien Phu and people's war theory, and evaluate the implications of 'Bamboo Diplomacy' for modern small-nation diplomacy.
VN-HO-001.case_en: In 1941, Ho Chi Minh established the Vietnam Independence League (Viet Minh) in northern mountainous areas, uniting patriotic forces across all social classes. From March to July 1954, he supported Vo Nguyen Giap's command of the Dien Bien Phu campaign, which surrounded and annihilated over 16,000 French expeditionary troops (5 brigades), ending French colonial rule in Indochina. In July of that year, the Geneva Accords recognized independence for Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia. After the 1954 north-south division, he persisted in 'peaceful unification and democratic freedom' policy, promoting northern socialist construction and southern national liberation struggle. On September 2, 1969, before his death he left the words: 'My sole wish is that the country is independent, the people are happy, and the nation is unified.'
VN-HO-001.cross_cultural_impact: Southeast Asian independence leader, anti-colonial struggle icon, bamboo diplomacy pioneer

Step 3: Marginal Thinking - Apply limited political resources to the critical few and key matters, decisively abandoning zero/negative marginal policies
Step 4: Mode 41/Stall System - Establish high-frequency information feedback loops, compressing policy signal transmission to monthly/quarterly levels

H-HLG-001.description_en: Hua Luogeng（1910-1985）: Hua Luogeng engineered 'independent autonomy' (mode 9) as 'mathematical self-reliance under credential deficit': under the fourfold constraint of junior-high dropout, permanent leg injury, no mentor, no laboratory, he bypassed the conventional 'study-abroad-for-degree' path and self-drawn a four-stage map of 'classic text mastery → core problem self-proof → frontier literature reproduction → open problem attack', using a single paper by Xiong Qinglin as a springboard to gain admission to Tsinghua via special exam; then produced 18 papers in two years at Cambridge — one sufficient for a PhD — instead of pursuing a degree. His famous words at Cambridge, 'I came for knowledge, not for a degree', epitomize the extreme case of 'self-defining success standards, refusing to be hostage to external credentials'.
H-HLG-001.reason_en: Core thinking modes: M9 (Independent Autonomy), M17 (Multidisciplinary Mental Models), M38 (Crossing the River by Feeling the Stones), M7 (Strategic Foresight). Hua Luogeng engineered 'independent autonomy' (mode 9) as self-reliance in mathematics under credential deficit: under the fourfold constraint of junior-high dropout, permanent leg injury, no mentor, and no laboratory, he bypassed the conventional 'study-abroad-for-degree' path and self-drawn a four-stage map of 'classic text mastery → core problem self-proof → frontier literature reproduction → open problem attack', gaining admission to Tsinghua via special exam with a single paper by Xiong Qinglin; then produced 18 papers in two years at Cambridge — one sufficient for a PhD — instead of pursuing a degree. He deployed 'multidisciplinary mental models' (mode 17) to distill 'analogy, induction, extremal principles, symmetry, invariants' into a reusable mathematical toolbox, translated for non-mathematicians; 'crossing the river by feeling the stones' (mode 38) to carry the golden-section/0.618 method from theory into chemical/metallurgical/agricultural sites, one-factory-one-strategy, using output-ratio as the green-light metric; and 'strategic foresight' (mode 7) to design a four-tier talent funnel of 'interest screening → ability testing → mentorship → international competition', compressing talent development from 5–8 years with the Youth Academy. These four modes interlock into a 'self-study → research → popularisation → application' transferable scientific-engineering system — the hallmark of scaling individual genius into national mathematical capacity.
steps_en: Step 1: Self-Taught Shortest Path — Deploy 'independent autonomy' (mode 9) to anchor the meta-assumption that 'mathematical truth ≠ degree certificate', self-draw a four-stage map of 'classic text mastery → core problem self-proof → frontier literature reproduction → open problem attack', and use hard output (18 Cambridge papers) to substitute for external credentials

Step 2: Methodological Toolisation — Deploy 'multidisciplinary mental models' (mode 17) to distil 'analogy, induction, extremal principles, symmetry, invariants' into a reusable mathematical toolkit, translated and opened for non-mathematicians such as engineers, agronomists, and workers

Step 3: Optimisation On-Site — Deploy 'crossing the river by feeling the stones' (mode 38) to carry the golden-section/0.618 method from theory into chemical, metallurgical, and agricultural sites, applying one-factory-one-strategy tuning, using 'output ratio increase of 20–50%' as a hard green-light gate for scaling

Step 4: Talent Funnel Screening — Deploy 'strategic foresight' (mode 7) to anticipate the trend that 'conventional schooling takes too long and top talent gets diluted', and design a four-tier funnel of 'interest screening → ability testing → mentorship → international competition' to compress talent development by 5–8 years via the Youth Academy

Step 5: Full-Chain Institutionalisation — Execute the 'mathematicalisation trinity': theoretical mathematisation (experience → formula) → applied mathematisation (craft → optimisation) → popularisation mathematisation (algorithm → workers), upgrading one-off breakthroughs into a 'self-study → research → popularisation → application' heritable scientific-engineering system

The Art of the Prime Numbers became a 20th-century classic in analytic number theory with Russian, Hungarian, Japanese, German, and English translations; internationally named results include the Hua–Walfisz theorem, Vinogradov–Hua theorem, and Hua's method

The optimising/unifying method was promoted across 20+ provinces; chemical, metallurgical, and agricultural sites reported 20–50% output gains, transforming mathematics from a 'palace game' into a 'productive tool'

Founded the Hua Luogeng Mathematics Class and advanced theUSTC Young Talents Program; the four-tier funnel compressed development by 5–8 years, directly training leaders such as Chen Jingrun, Wang Yuan, Lu Qikeng, Wan Zhexian, Gengsheng, and Tiangang

Named one of the 88 greatest mathematicians of our time by the Chicago Museum of Science and Technology; the third exemplar of mode 9 strengthening 'scientific self-reliance', and a low-frequency reinforcement of modes 17 and 7
H-HLG-001.case_en: 1910–1985: A panoramic view of Hua Luogeng's thinking-mode trajectory. Born Nov 12, 1910 in Jintan, Jiangsu; in 1925 he left Jintan County Primary School due to poverty — his only formal credential was a junior-high diploma, which he carried his whole life. In 1929 he contracted typhoid and permanently injured his left leg; walking with a cane, he still persisted in self-study and completed high-school through early-undergraduate mathematics in five years on his own. In 1930 he published 'On the Impossibility of Cardano's Algebraic Solution to the Quintic' in Science magazine; Tsinghua math chair Xiong Qinglin was so impressed he gave Hua a special-admission recommendation, bringing Hua to Tsinghua as a librarian in 1931 and promoting him — on three separate occasions — from assistant (1933) to lecturer (1934). In 1936, on Wiener's recommendation, he went to Cambridge but declined a PhD: 'I came for knowledge, not for a degree'; within two years he published 18 papers (10 in top-tier journals such as Proc. London Math. Soc. and Math. Ann.), and the 'Hua–Walfisz theorem' and 'Vinogradov–Hua theorem' bear his name, with Hardy lamenting 'My paper can never be the same again'. In 1938 he returned to China (turning down Cambridge continuation), became a professor at Southwest United University, and completed The Art of the Prime Numbers in a Kunming attic in 1942 (published by the Chinese Academy of Sciences in 1953, translated into Russian, Hungarian, Japanese, German, and English); this established the Chinese school of analytic number theory. In 1950 he declined a lifelong professorship at the University of Illinois to return, becoming chair of Tsinghua's Math Department (1950) and the founding director of the Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Mathematics (1952); his 1956 paper on harmonic analysis in typical domains of several complex variables won the National Natural Science Award, First Class. Starting in 1964 he led a small team to promote the 'optimising/unifying method' nationwide, reaching over 20 provinces with a single mass broadcast lecture in Wuhan attended by 600,000 people; in 1970 he was summoned by the State Council to instruct seven ministries on the dual method. In 1978 he founded the Hua Luogeng Mathematics Class and in 1985 helped create the USTC Youth Academy, designing a four-tier funnel — interest screening → ability testing → mentorship → international competition — that directly produced mathematical leaders such as Tian Gang, Zhu Qixia, Chen Xiaoxu, Chen Jingrun, Wang Yuan, Lu Qikeng, Wan Zhexian, and Gengsheng. He passed away of acute myocardial infarction while lecturing at the University of Tokyo on June 12, 1985, at age 74; he is counted among the 88 greatest mathematicians of our time by the Chicago Museum of Science and Technology.

H-LZ-001.reason: Li Zhi constructed a comprehensive anti-authority critical system centered on the Childlike Mind Theory, integrating individual authenticity, intellectual freedom, and material practice. He is the most complete case in Protreptic for anti-tradition and thought liberation.
steps: Step 1: Childlike Mind Foundation (M01) — Return to the 'first unfiltered thought' uncorrupted by dogma, use absolute authenticity as the starting point for value judgment
Step 2: Material Foundation (M02) — Confirm basic survival needs as the foundation of all values, reject empty speculation about metaphysical principles
Step 3: Heterodox Stance (M03) — Actively embrace marginal identity, transform critic's position into cognitive advantage
Step 4: Authenticity Test (M04) — Use inner genuine emotion as moral judgment standard, expose hypocrisy of inconsistent words and deeds
Step 5: Thought Liberation (M05) — Question the absolute authority of established norms, restore individual right to independent thinking
Step 6: Practical Verification (M06) — Test theories by actual utility, emphasize statecraft over empty talk
Step 7: Individual Expression (M07) — Affirm individual unique value, oppose standardized personality molding
Step 8: Equality Principle (M08) — Break down hierarchical distinctions, affirm women's wisdom and capabilities
Step 9: Conforming to Nature (M09) — Acknowledge legitimacy of natural desires, design systems that conform to human nature
Step 10: Dynamic History (M10) — Replace classical eternalism with 'progressive history' worldview
expected: Establish a complete anti-tradition thought system centered on Childlike Mind Theory
Become the theoretical banner of late Ming intellectual enlightenment movement
Profoundly influence Japan's Meiji Restoration
Provide systematic methodology for critical thinking
Pioneer individual liberation in Chinese intellectual history
H-LZ-001.case: Li Zhi wrote 'On Old Farmers and Gardeners' at age twelve, satirizing Confucius's view that farmers are petty people; passed the provincial exam in his twenties but held low-ranking posts for decades, deeply influenced by Wang Yangming's philosophy and the Taizhou School; retired late in life and settled at Zhifo Monastery in Macheng, writing and teaching for over a decade; propounded revolutionary ideas including Childlike Mind Theory and 'dressing and eating constitute human ethics'; praised Qin Shi Huang as 'emperor of the ages' and Wu Zetian as 'sage queen' in 'Records to Be Hidden'; vehemently attacked Neo-Confucian hypocrites in 'Books That Burn'; arrested in 1602 for 'propagating subversive doctrines' and committed suicide with a razor, saying 'a hero remembers not to lie unburied in ditches.' His thought influenced the late Ming Gong'an School, Japan's Meiji Restoration pioneer Yoshida Shoin, and Ray Huang's '1587, A Year of No Significance.'
H-LZ-001.description_en: [已完成] Li Zhi (1527-1602), prominent Ming Dynasty thinker, writer, and historian. Originally surnamed Lin, later changed to Li, courtesy name Hongfu, pseudonym Zhuo Wu. From Jinjiang, Quanzhou, Fujian, born into a maritime trade family. Deeply influenced by Wang Yangming's philosophy and the Taizhou School, he openly identified as a 'heterodox' thinker, propounding the Childlike Mind Theory and 'dressing and eating constitute human ethics,' critiquing Cheng-Zhu Neo-Confucianism and Confucian orthodoxy, advocating intellectual freedom and individual expression. Major works include 'Books That Burn,' 'Records to Be Hidden,' etc. Arrested in 1602 for 'subversive doctrines,' he committed suicide aged 76. His thought profoundly influenced late Ming enlightenment, Japan's Meiji Restoration, and China's May Fourth Movement.
